answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The whisper multiplier is published, charged in violet, and horizon lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1018 identities would post 1788 proofs and burn roughly 10 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
